title: Inappropriate Static Method Envy
pattern: A helper class defines a static/associated method that gets all of its input data from its arguments, performing calculations solely on the properties of a single passed-in object.
why_bad: It prevents polymorphism. If we want to implement different payment algorithms (such as `StraightTimeCalculator` or `OvertimeCalculator`), we cannot easily do so because the method is bound statically to an unrelated utility class.
detection: Statically dispatched methods that do not use any local self/state and operate exclusively on one of the passed parameters.
counterexample: Mathematical functions like `f64::max(a, b)` where there is no logical "owning" object and no desire for polymorphism.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 17 (G18 / G14).
